summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) has heated up again after a tense pause: UKMTO reported a tanker attacked north of Oman's Khasab on Nov 17, Oman evacuated its crew with one Indian sailor reported missing, and a US military official told Reuters that US aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island. Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian aerial attacks after Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US radar system there, and Iran's and Oman's foreign ministers discussed keeping shipping routes open in Muscat, with no agreement announced.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera).

status.label: The war
status.note: A US military official told Reuters that US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island on Nov 17, after earlier limited US strikes there on Nov 2 and Nov 7 and on launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik over Nov 15-16 (Euronews). On Nov 17 Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US radar system in Bahrain with drones; Bahrain said it intercepted the attacks. Qatar, a mediator, called for restraint; no deal has been signed.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent futures were hovering below US$90 a barrel on Wednesday, Nov 18, their lowest since late August (Yahoo Finance); WTI December futures were at US$82.62, down 2.4%, late in the morning (Yahoo Finance).

updates.text: UKMTO counted 308 vessel crossings of the Strait in the seven days to Nov 11 (139 outbound, 169 inbound), with shipping about 65% below pre-war levels (Al Jazeera, citing UKMTO).
sources: Al Jazeera: Is the strait really open?

updates.text: Iran's army said on Nov 18 that its drones targeted Patriot systems at Kuwait's Ali Al-Salem Air Base (state TV IRIB); CENTCOM said Iranian one-way drones were intercepted with no damage to US equipment and no US injuries.
sources: Gulf News live: Iran targets Bahrain, Adnoc vessel attacked, US strikes Qeshm

updates.text: GCC Secretary General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi condemned what he called repeated Iranian attacks on Bahrain and urged the UN Security Council to act.
sources: Gulf News live: Iran targets Bahrain, Adnoc vessel attacked, US strikes Qeshm

updates.text: On Nov 18 Bahrain's interior ministry warned of a "potential threat" and told residents to move to the nearest safe location, and Kuwait's army said its air defences were countering hostile drone attacks.
sources: The Times of Israel live blog, Nov 18

updates.text: Adnoc L&S said on Nov 18 that one of its ships was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening; one crew member is missing and eleven were injured, and the rest were evacuated.
sources: The National: Adnoc L&S ship attacked at Strait of Hormuz with one crew member missing

updates.who: Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao
updates.text: Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao told a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing on Nov 17 that insuring one Strait of Hormuz transit now costs $64 million, up from $54,000 before the war; Al Jazeera said the figure has not been independently verified.
sources: Al Jazeera: US official says Hormuz insurance hits $64m: Is the strait really open?

updates.text: Kuwait reported drone attacks on Nov 17, the same day Iran and the US traded strikes on Qeshm Island and Bahrain.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
